paragraphs: Roof bolters, mining, first verify underground roof and rib condition, gas, and ventilation, then position the roof bolting machine, drill holes, install bolts, and check tension; for loose rock, roof anomalies, gas, or guarding failure they stop work and escalate per mine procedures.

Continuous mining machine operators handle extraction, underground loading and haulage machine operators handle material transport, drillers handle formation drilling, and mining engineers handle design and safety systems. Roof bolters deliver roof support installed per plan and recorded.

AI can help organize support drawings, equipment inspections, and bolt records, but cannot independently determine roof stability, gas, ventilation, hole positions, bolt tension, or personnel refuge; underground actions must be performed by trained and authorized personnel.

This page is based on O*NET occupational tasks and fictional practice and does not predict personal suitability; underground mine work, gas detection, ventilation, and equipment authorization must be verified per location and employer procedures.

The BLS 2025 median annual wage for U.S. roof bolters, mining, is 78,540 U.S. dollars; 2025—2035 employment falls from about 2,200 to 1,800, a decline of 18.9%, with about 100 annual openings. Chinese mining wages serve only as industry background, and precise occupational wages were not obtained.

Roof bolters, mining (O*NET 47-5043.00) operate roof bolting machines underground: inspect the roof and ribs, verify gas and ventilation, position the machine, drill bolt holes, install resin or mechanical bolts, and measure tension and record per plan. Coal extraction, loading, or blasting duties must not be automatically assigned to this position.

O*NET 47-5043.00 provides roof bolter tasks and work activities; the BLS 2025—2035 occupational projections table for 47-5043 gives employment and median annual wages, and the O*NET national wage page gives BLS 2025 percentiles. The survey scope, period, and occupational codes of different statistical programs must be labeled separately.
